intro: Fiji is a nation of over 300 islands where Melanesian and Polynesian cultures meet, and it is a rugby sevens superpower.

chapters.title: Lapita voyagers
text: Lapita people, famous for decorated pottery, settled Fiji about 3,000 years ago. Fijian chiefs ruled powerful confederacies.

chapters.title: British rule and indenture
text: Chief Seru Cakobau ceded Fiji to Britain in 1874. Britain brought about 60,000 indentured workers from India to work sugar plantations from 1879.

highlight.title: Two communities
highlight.text: Indigenous Fijians (iTaukei) and Indo-Fijians shape the country today.

chapters.title: Independence and coups
text: Fiji became independent in 1970. Tensions between iTaukei and Indo-Fijians led to coups in 1987, 2000 and 2006. Democracy returned in 2014, and in 2022 power changed peacefully.

keyTerms.meaning: A ceremonial drink made from a pepper plant root.
